name: Le Studio French
summary: A client-side French speaking PWA built around a placement test and a twelve-unit roadmap. Every practice activity — conversation, dictation, spaced cards, quick fire, grammar, reading and listening — sits on the same progress model.

authorship.role: Sole author — learning path, activity types and progress model.
built: The twelve-unit, sixty-lesson roadmap and the CEFR placement test that calibrates it
The Today / Speak / Review / Learn / Progress navigation and the redo loop
Mock mode, which makes the entire app explorable offline with no API key
Key validation against the provider's models endpoint before anything is stored
notBuilt: Groq's hosted speech-to-text and text-to-speech, used for the speaking arena

caseStudy.problem: Language apps either drill vocabulary you never speak or drop you into conversation with no scaffolding. The gap is a path: something that knows roughly where you are, gives you a mixed diet of activities, and lets you redo the thing you just failed rather than moving on regardless.
caseStudy.approach: Start with a twelve-question placement test across A1–C2 and generate a personal roadmap where every unit mixes speaking with at least one grammar, reading or listening lesson. Keep the interface English-first so the scaffolding is never itself an obstacle, and put translations permanently within reach. Run entirely client-side, with the API key held only in local storage.

visuals.alt: Illustration of a French practice prompt with a translation panel and lesson progress
visuals.caption: Illustration of a practice session. Not a screenshot — no capture of the running app has been published yet.

metrics.label: Learning path
metrics.method: Counted from the shipped roadmap content; the placement test is 12 questions and calibrates AI complexity and scoring.

outcomes.statement: The whole app is explorable offline through mock mode, with no API key and no backend of any kind.
An entered API key is validated against the provider's models endpoint before being stored, so a bad key fails at setup rather than mid-session.

tradeoffs.choice: 100% client-side with a user-supplied API key
tradeoffs.gained: No backend, no accounts, no cost to run, and the key never leaves the user's browser.
tradeoffs.gaveUp: The user has to obtain and paste their own key, which is a hard first step for a non-technical learner.

limitations: No learner-progress study exists; fluency improvement is not measured and is graded 'insufficient-evidence' in the ecosystem's evidence registry.
Groq STT/TTS correction accuracy has never been benchmarked.
The API key lives in localStorage by design for a private tool — not hardened for public deployment.
